chunks: We praise Him for what has happened, and seek His succour in our affairs for what is yet to happen, and we beg Him for safety in the debts, just as we beg Him for safety in our bodies.

key_terms.مَا يَكُونُ: what is yet to happen (future events)

ai.seo_question: What does the supplication in Nahj al-Balagha say about seeking safety from debts?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) highlights the spiritual burden of debt (al-adyan) by equating it with physical well-being (al-abdan), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that financial obligations can hinder one's devotion and peace of mind. This supplication, found in the 'Abstinence of the World' chapter, underscores the holistic nature of divine protection, urging believers to seek relief from both material and spiritual constraints to maintain steadfastness in faith.
